subtitulo: Register on six axes: explaining investment
descripcion: At C2 register is controlled across six independent axes at once — contractions, vocabulary, sentence length, person, hedging and idiom — rather than as a single formal/informal switch, which is what lets a writer produce a genuinely intermediate register instead of an inconsistent mix.

filas: it may be the case that

ejemplos.texto: It's worth noting that the figures, while broadly accurate, don't tell the whole story.
I guess what I'm saying is that the evidence doesn't fully support the conclusion.
One might reasonably question whether this holds up under scrutiny.

notas: A genuinely intermediate register mixes some axes towards formal and others towards informal on purpose — for example, contractions kept but vocabulary raised — which reads as a controlled voice, not an inconsistency.
Moving all six axes together produces the two familiar extremes; moving them independently is what a mature, individual style actually sounds like.

An uncontrolled mix (contraction plus a very formal Latinate verb in the same clause, with no reason) is what a lower-level register error looks like — the difference from a controlled intermediate register is intentionality.

es.en: Spanish can mark register through tú/usted, which English lacks, so English register has to be carried entirely by vocabulary, contractions, sentence length and structure. Spanish speakers need to check these other axes consciously.
es.es: El español puede marcar el registro mediante «tú/usted», algo que el inglés no tiene. Por eso, en inglés el registro debe expresarse íntegramente mediante vocabulario, contracciones, longitud de las oraciones y estructura. Los hispanohablantes deben revisar conscientemente esos otros ejes.

de.en: German can mark register through du/Sie, which English lacks, so English register rests entirely on vocabulary, contractions, sentence length and structure. English contractions work like German spoken reductions (gibt's, hab's) as a signal of informality.
de.de: Deutsch kann Register über «du/Sie» markieren, was dem Englischen fehlt. Englisches Register hängt daher vollständig von Wortschatz, Kontraktionen, Satzlänge und Struktur ab. Englische Kontraktionen funktionieren ähnlich wie gesprochene deutsche Verkürzungen («gibt's», «hab's») als Informalitätssignal.

it.en: Italian can mark register through tu/Lei, which English lacks, so English register rests on vocabulary, contractions, sentence length and structure. Italian speakers need to check these axes consciously.
it.it: L'italiano può marcare il registro tramite «tu/Lei», cosa che l'inglese non fa. Il registro inglese si basa quindi su lessico, contrazioni, lunghezza delle frasi e struttura; gli italofoni devono controllare consapevolmente questi assi.

fr.en: French can mark register through tu/vous, which English lacks, so English register rests on vocabulary, contractions, sentence length and structure. English contractions work much like dropping ne in spoken French as a signal of informality.
fr.fr: Le français peut marquer le registre par «tu/vous», ce que l'anglais n'a pas. Le registre anglais repose donc sur le vocabulaire, les contractions, la longueur des phrases et la structure. Les contractions anglaises jouent un rôle proche de la chute de «ne» à l'oral en français comme marque d'informalité.

pt.en: Portuguese can mark register through tu, você and o senhor, which English lacks, so English register rests on vocabulary, contractions, sentence length and structure. Portuguese speakers need to check these axes consciously.
pt.pt: O português pode marcar registro por meio de «tu», «você» e «o senhor/a senhora», algo que o inglês não possui. Por isso, o registro inglês depende de vocabulário, contrações, comprimento das frases e estrutura; falantes de português precisam verificar esses eixos conscientemente.

errores: Moving all six axes formal or informal together, producing a generic rather than individual register.
Mixing axes with no discernible pattern, which reads as inconsistency rather than a controlled voice.
Losing track of which axis is actually doing the work in a given sentence.

es: Treating long subordinate chains as the main marker of formality, as in Spanish, where English formality lives mainly in word choice.
de: Equating formality with German passive and nominal style: *The implementation of the measure will be effected* instead of *We will implement the measure*.
it: Treating long subordinate chains as the main marker of formality, as in Italian, where English formality lives mainly in word choice.

pt: Treating long subordinate chains as the main marker of formality, as in Portuguese, where English formality lives mainly in word choice.

mision.consigna: Explain compound interest three ways: to a child, to a colleague at lunch and in a bank's information leaflet.
requisitos: each version distinct on at least four axes
one axis kept identical across all three on purpose

microtareas.texto: Write one sentence about *volatility* at six register points.
Identify which axis you find hardest to control.
Record 2 minutes on why people *squander* savings — then 30 seconds as a leaflet.

autochequeo: Are the six axes moved independently, not all together?
Is there a discernible pattern to which axes are formal and which aren't?
Does the resulting register read as a controlled individual voice?
Would a careful reader sense intention rather than inconsistency?
Is at least one axis deliberately mismatched from the others?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on register control across contractions, vocabulary, sentence length, person, hedging and idiom. Check whether any mismatch reads as intentional or as an error. Do not rewrite the text.
